text:
Ana: :wave: Quick sync — I'm sketching a pilot recruitment + feedback cadence for the private-preview cohort. Need ops & research input. Goal: onboard ~8 customers over 6 weeks, get prompt/latency/rollback signals, and define go/no-go metrics. Thoughts?

Kevin: timeline sounds tight but doable. Can we split into 2 waves (4 + 4) so we can iterate on onboarding docs and the SDK sample?

Maya: agree on waves. Also want to lock down the UX checklist for the first-run experience (API keys, example prompts, streaming vs non-streaming). Small friction up front kills engagement.

Jonah: from CS perspective, prioritize customers who already use Redwood-hosted inference (faster onboarding) and those with strict latency SLAs — they'll give stronger signals on perf regressions.

Lina: for feedback loops I recommend: weekly short survey (3 Qs), biweekly 30m interview for the first 2 waves, and automated error/latency sampling from telemetry. Capture sample prompts for evals.

Ana: good — propose this recruitment filter: 1) production inference use, 2) willingness to run a ~1-hour integration, 3) can share ~100 sample prompts or a dataset slice, 4) agrees to fortnightly sync. Anyone want to suggest edits?

Kevin: add "1 contact for escalation" and "existing infra: cloud or VPC". Also we should tag customers by model family & seq length distribution for rollout matrix.

Maya: sample onboarding message draft (please critique):

```
Hi! Thanks for joining the Redwood private preview. Next steps: 1) register a trial key (link), 2) run the quickstart in <30m using our SDK, 3) paste 50 sample prompts in the shared doc, 4) opt into either weekly survey or interview. We'll sync in week 2 to review latency and logs.
```

Jonah: minor edit — call out production-safety checklist: data egress policy, KMS setup if needed, and an opt-out for logging. Legal may need that in writing.

Ana: noted — will add a short opt-in clause. Now the big one: success criteria (go/no-go). My draft:
- Engagement: 75% complete quickstart within 7 days (goal: >=6/8 active)
- Quality: no more than 2 customer-reported major regressions caused by changes during pilot window
- Latency: p95 inference latency within 1.5x of baseline for 90% of requests
- Cost profile: per-token cost +/- 20% of expected model profile after batching/quantization suggestions
- Rollout readiness: can do canary by model variant with automatic fallback

Kevin: p95 target OK but let's make it relative to each customer's baseline (some have long sequences). Also track request failure rate (<0.5%).

Lina: add a qualitative metric: average NPS > 6/10 from the short survey and at least 3 in-depth interviews reporting measurable improvements or acceptable tradeoffs.

Maya: for scope negotiation — recommend we freeze all major perf-impacting infra changes during each wave unless the change has a short rollback path. That helps isolate signals.

Ana: agreed. For instrumentation: ops-bot please drop a checklist for required traces/metrics we need from customer side and what Redwood will collect.

ops-bot: Checklist created: token-level latency, per-request failure code, model variant id, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, cold-start counts, sample prompts (anonymized). Sharing policy: only aggregated telemetry unless customer opts in.

Jonah: ops-bot item — add "sample of error traces (sanitized)" and an automated alert when error rate > 0.5% for 10m.

ops-bot: Added.

Ana: Recruitment channels: account execs + CS for warm pull, product blog + limited signup, and targeted outreach to previous beta customers. Incentives: early pricing, 3 months free Dedicated credits, and co-marketing offer. Any objections?

Kevin: no objections. We should also offer a short implementation fund ($X) to cover engineering time for deeper integrations.

Maya: co-marketing fine but ensure we get explicit permission for case studies.

Lina: interview guide questions — I'll draft and share. Key ask: examples where latency or cost blocked a feature; willingness to accept small quality delta for cost gains.

Ana: operational runbook items: onboarding doc, rollback playbook (what conditions trigger rollback), single-tenant vs shared model variant routing rules, and a weekly review template. I'll take the runbook + rollback. Kevin can you own SDK sample updates? Maya — onboarding UX copy + consent language? Jonah — CS handoff + SLA communications? Lina — interview guide + survey?

Kevin: yep I'll update SDK sample with streaming & non-streaming snippets and a quick perf baseline tool (script).

Maya: on it. I'll add the consent/blurb and a microsite checklist for customers.

Jonah: I'll prepare a CS playbook for the first 30 days and an escalation matrix.

Lina: I'll post the interview guide by EOD Thursday.

Ana: thanks. Next steps: I’ll draft the recruitment email and the shortscreen form, plus the week-by-week pilot schedule. Meet Friday 11am to finalize wave 1 invites. Please flag if you can't make it. :calendar: :thumbsup:

Kevin: +1 Friday 11 works.

Maya: I can make it.

Jonah: I'll be there.

Lina: yes.

Ana: perfect — will share the doc shortly. End thread.
